content.title: UCF coach Sytia Messer working to navigate challenging college landscape
content.text: Like many of her counterparts in women’s basketball, UCF coach Sytia Messer is still trying to figure out how best to navigate the tumultuous waters that are college athletics. To that point, it’s been nothing short of a tsunami over the past few years, with the transfer portal and name, image, and likeness (NIL) now adding impending revenue-sharing in the wake of the House settlement, creating a swirling mess of chaos. For Messer, who wrapped up her third season with the Knights, it’s certainly been challenging. Following a 12-18 season, including a 4-14 mark in the Big 12, UCF lost 10 of its 13 players, highlighted by the transfer of three starters: Kaitlin Peterson and Emely Rodriguez and forward Achol Akot. Peterson led the team in scoring with 21.4 points per game, while Rodriguez, a true freshman, was second with 11.9. Messer and her coaching staff went to work rebuilding the roster, adding six players from the portal, led by Miami guard Leah Harmon along with Savannah Scott (Auburn), Audreonia Benson (Pensacola State College), Kristol Ayson (Tulsa), Jacorriah Bracey (Southern Miss) and Jasmynne Gibson (North Florida). Mahogany Chandler-Roberts, Khyala Ngodu and Summer Yancy return to round out the lineup. “We’re excited about the new additions. It’s always good to be able to start from scratch and to be able to start your own era,” Messer said during last week’s Big 12 spring meetings in Orlando. “Mahogany led us in offensive rebounds, and she’s just a sophomore. Khyala led us in rebounding, and she’s just a junior. So, we’re excited about that and adding on some talent,” she added. “We were able to get a point guard, Leah, out of the University of Miami, and it’s the first time we feel like we’ve had a true point guard in a few years. We’ll be about to lean on her and her experiences. We’re excited about the future.” Messer said throughout the process, there are three things she looks for when flipping a roster. “I look for character, academics and basketball,” she said. “I want to ensure, as we’re flipping the roster, that we’re getting kids in here with good character. We have to make sure we’re competing and doing the right things in the classroom and winning games.” Roster retention, meanwhile, has become particularly challenging in this day and age. Peterson transferred to Ole Miss, while Rodriguez landed at Iowa and Akol at Oklahoma State. “It was a lot about what prospects felt that was best for them and their family when it came to dollars and cents,” Messer said. “The kids, we wish them the best in that they had to do what was best for them and their families; we wish them nothing but the best.” The addition of the financial component in recent years, whether through NIL deals or collectives, has undoubtedly made building and maintaining a roster more challenging. Messer acknowledges that this shift has changed how she approaches potential future Knights. “The number one thing you’ve got to figure out what’s important to those kids and two, you have to figure out what is their non-negotiables,” she explains. “If we can’t meet that financially from the beginning, then we have to move on.” Despite finishing 13th last season, Messer believes it’s going to take time for the Knights to find their way in the Big 12. “This is our third year in the Big 12. We had predicted that the women’s basketball team would finish lower than it did, but it finished higher than expected. So that’s an improvement,” Messer explained. UCF was projected to finish 14th in the preseason poll, voted on by coaches. “Every year, you’ve got to get better and better, and that’s that’ll take time, but we’re going to keep working hard and bringing the right prospects in here,” she added.
